"PROJECT: ANIME RUSH — MULTIVERSE ESCAPE

1. YOUR ROLE AND PRIMARY OBJECTIVE

Act as a senior professional game developer, gameplay programmer, 3D game engineer, UI/UX designer, animation engineer, and mobile game optimization specialist.

Your task is to BUILD, IMPLEMENT, AND TEST a complete, professional-quality, fully functional endless runner action game titled:

ANIME RUSH: MULTIVERSE ESCAPE

This must be a genuine playable game, not a static visual prototype, landing page, animated background, or collection of decorative UI elements.

The game should combine the addictive three-lane endless runner mechanics of Subway Surfers with original anime-inspired environments, characters, combat abilities, boss encounters, and progression systems.

The game must be designed primarily for Android mobile phones, while also supporting desktop browsers.

CRITICAL DEVELOPMENT INSTRUCTION

Do not merely generate a visually attractive interface or claim that features have been implemented.

Actually implement the underlying functionality.

Every button must perform its intended action. Every character must be playable. Every obstacle must interact with the player. Every animation must work. Every gameplay system must be connected to the main game loop.

Do not replace functional gameplay with static images or decorative animations.

---

2. GAME GENRE AND CORE CONCEPT

Genre:

- Endless Runner
- Anime Action
- Survival
- Combat
- Boss Battles

Game Mode: Single Player.

Platform Priority:

1. Android smartphones
2. Mobile browsers
3. Desktop browsers

The player selects an anime character and enters that character's universe.

A powerful enemy from the selected universe continuously chases the player.

The player must:

- Run automatically.
- Avoid obstacles.
- Change lanes.
- Jump and slide.
- Collect coins and energy shards.
- Activate special abilities.
- Escape the chasing enemy.
- Defeat bosses at specific milestones.
- Unlock characters, abilities, skins, and universes.

There must be NO trains, railway tracks, subway stations, or conventional Subway Surfers environments.

The game must have its own identity, visual language, mechanics, and progression system.

---

3. CHARACTER SELECTION SYSTEM

Create a fully functional character selection screen.

Initially available characters should include:

Naruto Universe

1. Naruto Uzumaki
2. Adult Sasuke Uchiha
3. Kurama

Jujutsu Kaisen Universe

4. Yuji Itadori
5. Ryomen Sukuna
6. Satoru Gojo

Demon Slayer Universe

7. Tanjiro Kamado
8. Nezuko Kamado
9. Inosuke Hashibira
10. Zenitsu Agatsuma

One Punch Man Universe

11. Saitama
12. Genos
13. Tatsumaki

Additional characters can be introduced through future updates.

Character Selection Requirements

Each character must have:

- High-quality character artwork.
- A distinct visual appearance.
- An individual character preview.
- An animated idle pose where assets permit.
- Character name and anime universe.
- Character-specific statistics.
- Unique abilities.
- Unlock status.
- Selection indicator.

The selected character must actually appear in gameplay.

Do not use the same generic character model for every selection.

Use properly licensed assets, original assets, or permitted character-inspired artwork. Do not rely on missing external image URLs.

If an animated 3D model is unavailable, use a properly implemented 2D skeletal or sprite animation system with multiple animation frames. Never substitute a single static portrait for the actual player character.

---

4. UNIVERSE SELECTION AND ENVIRONMENT SYSTEM

Create a separate universe selection interface.

Every universe must have a visually distinct environment, lighting, architecture, obstacles, enemies, atmosphere, and soundtrack.

A. NARUTO UNIVERSE

Environments:

- Hidden Leaf Village
- Shinobi War Battlefield
- Forest of Death
- Destroyed Ninja Village

Enemies:

- Rogue Ninjas
- Akatsuki-inspired enemies
- Tailed Beasts
- Powerful Shinobi Bosses

Abilities:

- Rasengan Dash
- Shadow Clone Technique
- Susanoo Shield
- Kurama Chakra Boost

B. JUJUTSU KAISEN UNIVERSE

Environments:

- Cursed City
- Abandoned School
- Dark Battlefield
- Shibuya-inspired City

Enemies:

- Cursed Spirits
- Shikigami
- Special Grade Curses
- Powerful Cursed Bosses

Abilities:

- Black Flash Burst
- Domain Expansion
- Infinity Shield
- Cursed Energy Dash

C. DEMON SLAYER UNIVERSE

Environments:

- Dark Forest
- Traditional Japanese Village
- Demon Castle
- Mountain Battlefield

Enemies:

- Ordinary Demons
- Upper Moon Demons
- Powerful Demon Bosses

Abilities:

- Water Breathing Dash
- Thunderclap and Flash
- Flame Breathing
- Demon Rage Mode

D. ONE PUNCH MAN UNIVERSE

Environments:

- Destroyed City
- Monster Battlefield
- Alien Spaceship Environment
- Futuristic City

Enemies:

- Monsters
- Alien Warriors
- Powerful Mutants
- Dragon-Level Threats

Abilities:

- One Punch Finish
- Incineration Cannon
- Psychic Storm
- Serious Mode

Dynamic Environment Switching

The selected universe must determine:

- Environment models and textures.
- Background scenery.
- Ground materials.
- Lighting and atmosphere.
- Obstacle categories.
- Enemy selection.
- Boss encounters.
- Soundtrack.
- Visual effects.

Changing the selected character or universe must correctly update the gameplay environment.

Do not simply change the background image while leaving all other gameplay elements unchanged.

---

5. CORE ENDLESS RUNNER GAMEPLAY ENGINE

THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT PART OF THE PROJECT.

Implement a genuine three-lane endless runner system.

The player must automatically run forward while the environment and gameplay objects move relative to the player.

The player must remain visible and animated throughout gameplay.

Three-Lane System

Create three distinct lanes:

- Left Lane
- Middle Lane
- Right Lane

Implement smooth lane switching using interpolated movement.

The character must move between lanes without teleporting or instantly changing positions.

Movement Controls

Mobile:

- Swipe left: Move one lane left.
- Swipe right: Move one lane right.
- Swipe up: Jump.
- Swipe down: Slide.
- Tap ability button: Activate selected ability.

Desktop:

- Left Arrow / A: Move left.
- Right Arrow / D: Move right.
- Up Arrow / W: Jump.
- Down Arrow / S: Slide.
- Space: Activate Ultimate Mode.

Movement Requirements

Implement:

- Automatic forward movement.
- Smooth lane switching.
- Jumping with a proper jump arc.
- Sliding with a defined duration.
- Landing detection.
- Movement restrictions at lane boundaries.
- Frame-rate-independent movement.
- Responsive input handling.
- Proper movement state management.

Use delta-time-based calculations.

Do not make the player move at different speeds depending on the device's frame rate.

---

6. REAL CHARACTER ANIMATION SYSTEM

A static character image is NOT acceptable.

Implement actual animation states.

Required animations:

1. Idle
2. Running
3. Jumping
4. Falling
5. Sliding
6. Taking Damage
7. Ability Activation
8. Ultimate Transformation
9. Boss Attack
10. Death / Game Over

Animations should transition smoothly.

Use:

- Sprite sheets with multiple frames.
- Skeletal animation.
- Animated 3D models.
- Animation blending where supported.

The character must visibly animate while running.

Jumping must display a different animation from running.

Sliding must visibly change the character's posture.

Damage and ability activation must produce appropriate animation and visual feedback.

Ensure that animation states are controlled by actual gameplay events.

---

7. REAL PHYSICS AND COLLISION SYSTEM

Implement a proper physics and collision system.

Requirements:

- Gravity.
- Jump velocity.
- Ground detection.
- Jump arc.
- Landing detection.
- Player collider.
- Obstacle colliders.
- Enemy collision detection.
- Power-up collection detection.
- Boss interaction detection.

Use a suitable physics engine or a properly implemented collision system.

All movement and collision calculations must be frame-rate independent.

Prevent:

- Passing through obstacles.
- Incorrect collision detection.
- Multiple collision triggers from one obstacle.
- Jumping while already airborne, unless explicitly supported.
- Sliding and jumping state conflicts.

Collision Consequences

When the player collides with an obstacle:

- Play a hit animation.
- Display a collision effect.
- Play an appropriate sound.
- Reduce health or increase the chaser's proximity.
- Apply a temporary slowdown if appropriate.

Allow a limited number of mistakes before Game Over.

Use a short invulnerability period after damage to prevent repeated collision registration.

---

8. PROCEDURAL OBSTACLE GENERATION

Create a genuine procedural obstacle generation system.

Obstacles must continuously spawn ahead of the player.

Examples:

Naruto:

- Fallen trees.
- Broken structures.
- Chakra barriers.
- Battlefield debris.

Jujutsu Kaisen:

- Destroyed buildings.
- Cursed barriers.
- Broken vehicles.
- Cursed energy hazards.

Demon Slayer:

- Fallen trees.
- Rock formations.
- Wooden barriers.
- Demon-created hazards.

One Punch Man:

- Destroyed buildings.
- Concrete blocks.
- Alien debris.
- Monster hazards.

Obstacle Types

1. Ground obstacles requiring jumping.
2. Overhead obstacles requiring sliding.
3. Full-lane obstacles requiring lane switching.
4. Moving obstacles.
5. Special hazards.

Each obstacle must have:

- Collision detection.
- Correct lane positioning.
- Spawn timing.
- Despawn logic.
- Visual feedback.
- Appropriate interaction.

Difficulty Progression

Gradually increase:

- Forward speed.
- Obstacle frequency.
- Obstacle combinations.
- Moving obstacle complexity.
- Enemy pressure.

Difficulty must increase progressively rather than suddenly becoming impossible.

Object Pooling

Implement object pooling for frequently spawned obstacles, coins, and effects.

Reuse objects instead of continuously creating and destroying them.

Prevent memory leaks and uncontrolled object accumulation.

---

9. CHASING ENEMY SYSTEM

A powerful enemy must continuously chase the player.

The chaser should be selected from the selected character's original universe.

Examples:

- Naruto: Tailed Beast or powerful rogue Shinobi.
- Yuji: Special Grade Curse.
- Tanjiro: Powerful Demon.
- Saitama: Monster or alien threat.

Chaser Behaviour

The enemy must:

- Spawn behind the player.
- Remain visible.
- Have a running or chasing animation.
- Follow the player dynamically.
- React to player collisions.
- Gradually approach after mistakes.
- Fall behind when the player performs well.

Display a visual chaser proximity indicator.

If the chaser catches the player, trigger Game Over.

The chaser must not be a static image placed behind the character.

Implement its actual movement and gameplay behaviour.

---

10. SPECIAL ABILITY SYSTEM

Every playable character must have individual abilities.

The ability system must be functional, not merely decorative.

Each ability should have:

- Activation input.
- Energy requirement or cooldown.
- Duration.
- Visual effect.
- Sound effect.
- Gameplay consequence.
- Cooldown indicator.

Examples:

Naruto:

- Rasengan Dash: Temporarily clears obstacles ahead.
- Shadow Clone: Provides temporary protection.
- Kurama Mode: Increases speed and grants temporary invulnerability.

Gojo:

- Infinity: Protects against collisions temporarily.
- Domain Expansion: Triggers a special visual effect and gameplay advantage.
- Cursed Energy Burst: Clears selected hazards.

Tanjiro:

- Water Breathing: Performs a powerful forward dash.
- Thunderclap-style movement: Provides a short speed boost.
- Demon Slayer Focus: Temporarily improves protection.

Saitama:

- One Punch: Clears eligible obstacles or defeats selected enemies.
- Serious Mode: Provides a temporary powerful state.

Genos:

- Incineration Cannon: Clears obstacles within its defined range.

Tatsumaki:

- Psychic Storm: Removes or suspends eligible obstacles.

Abilities must be balanced and must not create unintended permanent invincibility.

---

11. ENERGY AND ULTIMATE MODE

Implement an energy collection system.

Players collect energy shards during runs.

Energy must increase according to actual collected items.

When the energy meter reaches 100%, the Ultimate Mode button becomes available.

Upon activation:

- Character enters a powered-up form.
- Special aura surrounds the character.
- Running speed increases.
- Temporary invulnerability is activated.
- Cinematic visual effects appear.
- The soundtrack changes temporarily.
- Special animation plays.

Each character must have a unique Ultimate Mode appearance and effect.

After the duration expires, return to normal gameplay.

The energy meter must reset or decrease according to the defined game rules.

---

12. COINS, POWER-UPS AND COLLECTIBLES

Implement collectible objects throughout the running environment.

Collectibles

- Gold Coins.
- Energy Shards.
- Health Recovery Items.
- Speed Boosts.
- Temporary Shields.
- Magnet Power-Ups.

Requirements

Every collectible must:

- Spawn dynamically.
- Be positioned in actual gameplay lanes.
- Have a collision or collection trigger.
- Disappear when collected.
- Update the relevant counter.
- Play a collection animation.
- Trigger an appropriate sound.

Coins must be saved and remain available after the player closes and reopens the game.

Use persistent storage supported by the target platform.

---

13. MINI-BOSS BATTLE SYSTEM

After every 2,000 meters, transition into a mini-boss encounter.

The normal running sequence should temporarily transition into a dedicated boss arena.

Each boss must have:

- Unique appearance.
- Health bar.
- Attack animations.
- Attack patterns.
- Damage detection.
- Defeat animation.
- Victory and defeat conditions.

The player must use abilities, dodging, and attacks to defeat the boss within a time limit.

The boss fight must be an actual interactive encounter.

It must not be a static boss image or an automatic victory animation.

Boss Rewards

Successful completion may reward:

- Rare character skins.
- Coins.
- Ability upgrades.
- New characters.
- Universe unlocks.

After the encounter, return to endless runner gameplay with the correct game state and difficulty.

---

14. GAME UI AND USER INTERFACE

Create a modern, premium anime-themed interface.

The UI must be clean, readable, responsive, and visually consistent.

Main Menu

Include:

- Game logo.
- Animated background.
- Play button.
- Character selection.
- Universe selection.
- Character collection.
- Upgrade section.
- Settings.
- Coins balance.
- Player profile.

Gameplay Interface

Display:

- Current score.
- Distance in meters.
- Coin counter.
- Energy meter.
- Health indicator.
- Chaser proximity.
- Ability button.
- Ultimate Mode button.
- Pause button.

Pause Menu

Include:

- Resume.
- Restart.
- Return to Main Menu.
- Sound settings.

Game Over Screen

Display:

- Final score.
- Distance travelled.
- Coins collected.
- Energy collected.
- Obstacles avoided.
- Bosses defeated.
- Best score.
- Retry button.
- Main Menu button.

UI Design Requirements

Use:

- Professional typography.
- Clear icons.
- Anime-inspired visual effects.
- Readable contrast.
- Smooth transitions.
- Appropriate spacing.
- Responsive layouts.

Do not use completely black backgrounds that hide interface elements.

Do not allow UI layers to block gameplay or touch controls.

Every visible button must be functional.

---

15. CHARACTER COLLECTION AND UPGRADE SYSTEM

Create a persistent progression system.

Players should be able to:

- Unlock characters.
- Purchase skins.
- Upgrade speed.
- Upgrade ability duration.
- Reduce cooldown.
- Increase starting protection.
- Unlock additional universes.

Every upgrade must produce a measurable gameplay effect.

Display:

- Current upgrade level.
- Upgrade cost.
- Current statistics.
- Improved statistics.
- Unlock requirements.

Do not create buttons that claim to purchase or upgrade something without actually changing the relevant game data.

---

16. AUDIO AND VISUAL EFFECTS

Audio

Implement:

- Main menu soundtrack.
- Universe-specific background music.
- Running sounds.
- Jump sounds.
- Slide sounds.
- Collision sounds.
- Coin collection sounds.
- Ability sounds.
- Boss battle music.
- Game Over sound.

Music should change appropriately between menus, running gameplay, Ultimate Mode, and boss encounters.

Provide independent music and sound effect volume controls.

Visual Effects

Implement:

- Anime-style aura effects.
- Motion trails.
- Energy particles.
- Speed effects.
- Impact effects.
- Landing effects.
- Ability animations.
- Ultimate transformation effects.
- Boss attack effects.

Use appropriate lighting and visual effects without sacrificing performance.

---

17. MOBILE-FIRST DEVELOPMENT

The game must be optimized primarily for Android smartphones.

Screen Orientation

Use portrait orientation (9:16) as the primary gameplay layout.

The game should occupy the available screen without unnecessary scrolling.

Mobile Controls

Implement reliable touch gesture detection.

Important:

- Detect swipe direction accurately.
- Avoid triggering multiple movements from one swipe.
- Prevent accidental browser scrolling during gameplay.
- Avoid conflicts between swipe controls and UI buttons.
- Provide responsive touch feedback.

Mobile UI

Position gameplay buttons where they are easily accessible.

Ensure:

- Score is readable.
- Energy bar is visible.
- Ability buttons are sufficiently large.
- Pause button is accessible.
- The character and obstacles remain visible.

Performance

Target smooth 60 FPS gameplay on capable mobile devices.

Use adaptive graphics settings for lower-end devices.

Optimize:

- Texture sizes.
- Model complexity.
- Draw calls.
- Particle counts.
- Memory consumption.
- Animation processing.
- Object spawning.

Avoid unnecessary rendering and excessive effects.

---

18. TECHNICAL ARCHITECTURE

Before implementation, inspect the existing project and identify its framework, rendering engine, dependencies, file structure, and existing assets.

Do not blindly overwrite working code.

Preserve useful existing functionality and rebuild broken systems properly.

Organize the project into logical modules.

Suggested architecture:

- GameManager
- GameStateManager
- PlayerController
- PlayerAnimationController
- PlayerPhysics
- LaneMovementController
- InputController
- ObstacleManager
- ObstaclePool
- CollisionManager
- EnemyChaserController
- AbilityManager
- UltimateModeManager
- CollectibleManager
- EnergyManager
- ScoreManager
- BossManager
- CharacterManager
- UniverseManager
- AudioManager
- CameraController
- UIManager
- SaveManager
- PerformanceManager

Use the architecture appropriate to the existing technology stack.

Main Game Loop

The game loop must correctly handle:

1. Reading player input.
2. Updating player movement.
3. Updating physics.
4. Updating animations.
5. Updating obstacle positions.
6. Spawning obstacles.
7. Updating enemy AI.
8. Checking collisions.
9. Updating collectibles.
10. Updating score and distance.
11. Updating energy and health.
12. Updating camera.
13. Rendering the scene.
14. Updating the UI.

Use delta time and proper game state management.

Game States

Implement these states:

- Loading
- Main Menu
- Character Selection
- Universe Selection
- Ready
- Playing
- Paused
- Boss Battle
- Game Over

Transitions must be handled correctly.

Prevent multiple simultaneous game loops.

Prevent gameplay updates while paused.

Restarting must reset the previous run's temporary objects, timers, score, collision states, and player physics.

---

19. CRITICAL BUG PREVENTION AND QUALITY ASSURANCE

Previous versions of this project repeatedly suffered from the following issues:

1. Completely black interfaces.
2. Missing character artwork.
3. Missing environment assets.
4. Start button not working.
5. Only the background appearing.
6. Static player character.
7. No running animation.
8. No actual movement.
9. No obstacles.
10. No collision detection.
11. No enemy chasing.
12. Broken mobile controls.
13. UI elements covering the gameplay.
14. Incorrect rendering order.
15. Missing asset references.
16. Runtime errors.
17. Incorrect initialization.
18. Restart button failing.
19. Gameplay freezing.
20. Excessive memory consumption.

These problems must be specifically tested for and eliminated.

Asset Loading

Implement:

- Asset preloading.
- Loading progress indicator.
- Asset validation.
- Error handling.
- Fallback assets.

Never allow a missing external image to turn the entire game screen black.

If an asset fails to load, use a visible fallback asset and report the problem.

Rendering Validation

Before starting a run, verify that:

- Renderer is initialized.
- Camera is active.
- Environment exists.
- Player exists.
- Player animation controller exists.
- Enemy exists.
- Game loop is active.
- Required UI elements are visible.

Do not start gameplay if essential systems have failed silently.

Functional Testing

Test the following:

TEST 1: Open the game and verify the main menu.

TEST 2: Open character selection and select different characters.

TEST 3: Change the universe and verify that the environment changes.

TEST 4: Press Start and verify that a playable character spawns.

TEST 5: Verify that running animation plays continuously.

TEST 6: Test all three lanes.

TEST 7: Test jumping and landing.

TEST 8: Test sliding.

TEST 9: Verify that obstacles spawn dynamically.

TEST 10: Verify that collision detection works.

TEST 11: Verify that the chasing enemy follows the player.

TEST 12: Collect coins and energy shards.

TEST 13: Activate character-specific abilities.

TEST 14: Fill the energy bar and activate Ultimate Mode.

TEST 15: Verify distance and score calculations.

TEST 16: Test pause and resume.

TEST 17: Test Game Over.

TEST 18: Test restart.

TEST 19: Test saving and loading progression.

TEST 20: Verify that the game works on a mobile screen.

Fix all discovered errors before considering the game complete.

---

20. DEVELOPMENT PRIORITIES

Implement the project in the following order.

PHASE 1 — FUNCTIONAL FOUNDATION

Build:

- Rendering engine.
- Main menu.
- Game state manager.
- Player spawning.
- Actual character movement.
- Running animation.
- Three-lane system.
- Jumping and sliding.
- Camera.

At the end of this phase, a complete basic endless runner must already be playable.

PHASE 2 — CORE GAMEPLAY

Build:

- Physics.
- Obstacles.
- Collision detection.
- Chasing enemy.
- Distance tracking.
- Score.
- Health.
- Game Over.
- Restart.

PHASE 3 — ANIME SYSTEMS

Build:

- Character selection.
- Universe selection.
- Universe-specific environments.
- Enemy variations.
- Character-specific animations.
- Special abilities.
- Ultimate Mode.

PHASE 4 — ADVANCED GAMEPLAY

Build:

- Coins.
- Energy shards.
- Power-ups.
- Boss encounters.
- Character collection.
- Upgrade system.
- Skins.
- Rewards.

PHASE 5 — POLISH AND OPTIMIZATION

Build:

- Professional UI.
- Soundtrack.
- Visual effects.
- Mobile controls.
- Responsive layouts.
- Performance optimization.
- Persistent saving.
- Final testing.

Do not skip the functional foundation in order to prioritize artwork or visual presentation.

---

21. FUTURE MULTIPLAYER EXPANSION

Design the architecture so multiplayer can be introduced later without rebuilding the entire game.

Potential future modes:

- 1v1 Survival Race.
- Team Escape.
- Cooperative Boss Raid.
- Global Leaderboards.

These features are future development goals and must not interfere with the quality of the current single-player version.

---

22. FINAL DELIVERY REQUIREMENTS

The final product must be a fully playable, properly implemented game.

When the user opens the project:

1. The main menu must load correctly.
2. Character selection must work.
3. Universe selection must work.
4. Start must load an actual gameplay scene.
5. The selected character must spawn and run automatically.
6. Running, jumping, and sliding animations must work.
7. All three lanes must be functional.
8. Obstacles must spawn dynamically.
9. Collision detection must work.
10. The chasing enemy must follow the player.
11. Coins and energy shards must be collectible.
12. Abilities must have real gameplay effects.
13. The score and distance must update continuously.
14. The pause and restart systems must work.
15. Game Over must function correctly.
16. Progression must be saved.
17. The game must work on Android mobile screens.

NON-NEGOTIABLE RULES

- Do not create a static visual mockup.
- Do not simulate gameplay using only background movement.
- Do not use a single static character image as the player.
- Do not create decorative buttons without functionality.
- Do not leave essential gameplay systems as placeholders.
- Do not claim that a feature works without implementing and testing it.
- Do not ignore runtime errors.
- Do not leave the game in a black-screen or incomplete state.
- Do not stop after creating the home screen.
- Do not sacrifice actual functionality for visual appearance.

If an advanced feature cannot be completed immediately, prioritize a functional implementation with clear limitations rather than displaying a fake feature.

FINAL INSTRUCTION

First inspect the existing project. Then implement the game systematically, beginning with a genuinely playable endless runner foundation.

After implementation, run the project, test the actual gameplay, identify errors, and fix them.

Do not merely provide an implementation plan, code snippets, screenshots, or a description of what you would build.

Modify the actual project files and deliver the working game.

The final result should feel like a polished, professional anime action game with smooth controls, genuine character animations, responsive gameplay, dynamic environments, exciting combat abilities, and a complete progression system.

Remember: A visually attractive game that cannot actually be played is a failed deliverable. Functionality, stability, and genuine gameplay take priority over everything else.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

9. Inosuke Hashibira
10. Zenitsu Agatsuma

One Punch Man Universe

11. Saitama
12. Genos
13. Tatsumaki

Additional characters can be introduced through future updates.

Character Selection Requirements

Each character must have:

- High-quality character artwork.
- A distinct visual appearance.
- An individual character preview.
- An animated idle pose where assets permit.
- Character name and anime universe.
- Character-specific statistics.
- Unique abilities.
- Unlock status.
- Selection indicator.

The selected character must actually appear in gameplay.

Do not use the same generic character model for every selection.

Use properly licensed assets, original assets, or permitted character-inspired artwork. Do not rely on missing external image URLs.

If an animated 3D model is unavailable, use a properly implemented 2D skeletal or sprite animation system with multiple animation frames. Never substitute a single static portrait for the actual player character.

---

4. UNIVERSE SELECTION AND ENVIRONMENT SYSTEM

Create a separate universe selection interface.

Every universe must have a visually distinct environment, lighting, architecture, obstacles, enemies, atmosphere, and soundtrack.

A. NARUTO UNIVERSE

Environments:

- Hidden Leaf Village
- Shinobi War Battlefield
- Forest of Death
- Destroyed Ninja Village

Enemies:

- Rogue Ninjas
- Akatsuki-inspired enemies
- Tailed Beasts
- Powerful Shinobi Bosses

Abilities:

- Rasengan Dash
- Shadow Clone Technique
- Susanoo Shield
- Kurama Chakra Boost

B. JUJUTSU KAISEN UNIVERSE

Environments:

- Cursed City
- Abandoned School
- Dark Battlefield
- Shibuya-inspired City

Enemies:

- Cursed Spirits
- Shikigami
- Special Grade Curses
- Powerful Cursed Bosses

Abilities:

- Black Flash Burst
- Domain Expansion
- Infinity Shield
- Cursed Energy Dash

C. DEMON SLAYER UNIVERSE

Environments:

- Dark Forest
- Traditional Japanese Village
- Demon Castle
- Mountain Battlefield

Enemies:

- Ordinary Demons
- Upper Moon Demons
- Powerful Demon Bosses

Abilities:

- Water Breathing Dash
- Thunderclap and Flash
- Flame Breathing
- Demon Rage Mode

D. ONE PUNCH MAN UNIVERSE

Environments:

- Destroyed City
- Monster Battlefield
- Alien Spaceship Environment
- Futuristic City

Enemies:

- Monsters
- Alien Warriors
- Powerful Mutants
- Dragon-Level Threats

Abilities:

- One Punch Finish
- Incineration Cannon
- Psychic Storm
- Serious Mode

Dynamic Environment Switching

The selected universe must determine:

- Environment models and textures.
- Background scenery.
- Ground materials.
- Lighting and atmosphere.
- Obstacle categories.
- Enemy selection.
- Boss encounters.
- Soundtrack.
- Visual effects.

Changing the selected character or universe must correctly update the gameplay environment.

Do not simply change the background image while leaving all other gameplay elements unchanged.

---

5. CORE ENDLESS RUNNER GAMEPLAY ENGINE

THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT PART OF THE PROJECT.

Implement a genuine three-lane endless runner system.

The player must automatically run forward while the environment and gameplay objects move relative to the player.

The player must remain visible and animated throughout gameplay.

Three-Lane System

Create three distinct lanes:

- Left Lane
- Middle Lane
- Right Lane

Implement smooth lane switching using interpolated movement.

The character must move between lanes without teleporting or instantly changing positions.

Movement Controls

Mobile:

- Swipe left: Move one lane left.
- Swipe right: Move one lane right.
- Swipe up: Jump.
- Swipe down: Slide.
- Tap ability button: Activate selected ability.

Desktop:

- Left Arrow / A: Move left.
- Right Arrow / D: Move right.
- Up Arrow / W: Jump.
- Down Arrow / S: Slide.
- Space: Activate Ultimate Mode.

Movement Requirements

Implement:

- Automatic forward movement.
- Smooth lane switching.
- Jumping with a proper jump arc.
- Sliding with a defined duration.
- Landing detection.
- Movement restrictions at lane boundaries.
- Frame-rate-independent movement.
- Responsive input handling.
- Proper movement state management.

Use delta-time-based calculations.

Do not make the player move at different speeds depending on the device's frame rate.

---

6. REAL CHARACTER ANIMATION SYSTEM

A static character image is NOT acceptable.

Implement actual animation states.

Required animations:

1. Idle
2. Running
3. Jumping
4. Falling
5. Sliding
6. Taking Damage
7. Ability Activation
8. Ultimate Transformation
9. Boss Attack
10. Death / Game Over

Animations should transition smoothly.

Use:

- Sprite sheets with multiple frames.
- Skeletal animation.
- Animated 3D models.
- Animation blending where supported.

The character must visibly animate while running.

Jumping must display a different animation from running.

Sliding must visibly change the character's posture.

Damage and ability activation must produce appropriate animation and visual feedback.

Ensure that animation states are controlled by actual gameplay events.

---

7. REAL PHYSICS AND COLLISION SYSTEM

Implement a proper physics and collision system.

Requirements:

- Gravity.
- Jump velocity.
- Ground detection.
- Jump arc.
- Landing detection.
- Player collider.
- Obstacle colliders.
- Enemy collision detection.
- Power-up collection detection.
- Boss interaction detection.

Use a suitable physics engine or a properly implemented collision system.

All movement and collision calculations must be frame-rate independent.

Prevent:

- Passing through obstacles.
- Incorrect collision detection.
- Multiple collision triggers from one obstacle.
- Jumping while already airborne, unless explicitly supported.
- Sliding and jumping state conflicts.

Collision Consequences

When the player collides with an obstacle:

- Play a hit animation.
- Display a collision effect.
- Play an appropriate sound.
- Reduce health or increase the chaser's proximity.
- Apply a temporary slowdown if appropriate.

Allow a limited number of mistakes before Game Over.

Use a short invulnerability period after damage to prevent repeated collision registration.

---

8. PROCEDURAL OBSTACLE GENERATION

Create a genuine procedural obstacle generation system.

Obstacles must continuously spawn ahead of the player.

Examples:

Naruto:

- Fallen trees.
- Broken structures.
- Chakra barriers.
- Battlefield debris.

Jujutsu Kaisen:

- Destroyed buildings.
- Cursed barriers.
- Broken vehicles.
- Cursed energy hazards.

Demon Slayer:

- Fallen trees.
- Rock formations.
- Wooden barriers.
- Demon-created hazards.

One Punch Man:

- Destroyed buildings.
- Concrete blocks.
- Alien debris.
- Monster hazards.

Obstacle Types

1. Ground obstacles requiring jumping.
2. Overhead obstacles requiring sliding.
3. Full-lane obstacles requiring lane switching.
4. Moving obstacles.
5. Special hazards.

Each obstacle must have:

- Collision detection.
- Correct lane positioning.
- Spawn timing.
- Despawn logic.
- Visual feedback.
- Appropriate interaction.

Difficulty Progression

Gradually increase:

- Forward speed.
- Obstacle frequency.
- Obstacle combinations.
- Moving obstacle complexity.
- Enemy pressure.

Difficulty must increase progressively rather than suddenly becoming impossible.

Object Pooling

Implement object pooling for frequently spawned obstacles, coins, and effects.

Reuse objects instead of continuously creating and destroying them.

Prevent memory leaks and uncontrolled object accumulation.

---

9. CHASING ENEMY SYSTEM

A powerful enemy must continuously chase the player.

The chaser should be selected from the selected character's original universe.

Examples:

- Naruto: Tailed Beast or powerful rogue Shinobi.
- Yuji: Special Grade Curse.
- Tanjiro: Powerful Demon.
- Saitama: Monster or alien threat.

Chaser Behaviour

The enemy must:

- Spawn behind the player.
- Remain visible.
- Have a running or chasing animation.
- Follow the player dynamically.
- React to player collisions.
- Gradually approach after mistakes.
- Fall behind when the player performs well.

Display a visual chaser proximity indicator.

If the chaser catches the player, trigger Game Over.

The chaser must not be a static image placed behind the character.

Implement its actual movement and gameplay behaviour.

---

10. SPECIAL ABILITY SYSTEM

Every playable character must have individual abilities.

The ability system must be functional, not merely decorative.

Each ability should have:

- Activation input.
- Energy requirement or cooldown.
- Duration.
- Visual effect.
- Sound effect.
- Gameplay consequence.
- Cooldown indicator.

Examples:

Naruto:

- Rasengan Dash: Temporarily clears obstacles ahead.
- Shadow Clone: Provides temporary protection.
- Kurama Mode: Increases speed and grants temporary invulnerability.

Gojo:

- Infinity: Protects against collisions temporarily.
- Domain Expansion: Triggers a special visual effect and gameplay advantage.
- Cursed Energy Burst: Clears selected hazards.

Tanjiro:

- Water Breathing: Performs a powerful forward dash.
- Thunderclap-style movement: Provides a short speed boost.
- Demon Slayer Focus: Temporarily improves protection.

Saitama:

- One Punch: Clears eligible obstacles or defeats selected enemies.
- Serious Mode: Provides a temporary powerful state.

Genos:

- Incineration Cannon: Clears obstacles within its defined range.

Tatsumaki:

- Psychic Storm: Removes or suspends eligible obstacles.

Abilities must be balanced and must not create unintended permanent invincibility.

---

11. ENERGY AND ULTIMATE MODE

Implement an energy collection system.

Players collect energy shards during runs.

Energy must increase according to actual collected items.

When the energy meter reaches 100%, the Ultimate Mode button becomes available.

Upon activation:

- Character enters a powered-up form.
- Special aura surrounds the character.
- Running speed increases.
- Temporary invulnerability is activated.
- Cinematic visual effects appear.
- The soundtrack changes temporarily.
- Special animation plays.

Each character must have a unique Ultimate Mode appearance and effect.

After the duration expires, return to normal gameplay.

The energy meter must reset or decrease according to the defined game rules.

---

12. COINS, POWER-UPS AND COLLECTIBLES

Implement collectible objects throughout the running environment.

Collectibles

- Gold Coins.
- Energy Shards.
- Health Recovery Items.
- Speed Boosts.
- Temporary Shields.
- Magnet Power-Ups.

Requirements

Every collectible must:

- Spawn dynamically.
- Be positioned in actual gameplay lanes.
- Have a collision or collection trigger.
- Disappear when collected.
- Update the relevant counter.
- Play a collection animation.
- Trigger an appropriate sound.

Coins must be saved and remain available after the player closes and reopens the game.

Use persistent storage supported by the target platform.

---

13. MINI-BOSS BATTLE SYSTEM

After every 2,000 meters, transition into a mini-boss encounter.

The normal running sequence should temporarily transition into a dedicated boss arena.

Each boss must have:

- Unique appearance.
- Health bar.
- Attack animations.
- Attack patterns.
- Damage detection.
- Defeat animation.
- Victory and defeat conditions.

The player must use abilities, dodging, and attacks to defeat the boss within a time limit.

The boss fight must be an actual interactive encounter.

It must not be a static boss image or an automatic victory animation.

Boss Rewards

Successful completion may reward:

- Rare character skins.
- Coins.
- Ability upgrades.
- New characters.
- Universe unlocks.

After the encounter, return to endless runner gameplay with the correct game state and difficulty.

---

14. GAME UI AND USER INTERFACE

Create a modern, premium anime-themed interface.

The UI must be clean, readable, responsive, and visually consistent.

Main Menu

Include:

- Game logo.
- Animated background.
- Play button.
- Character selection.
- Universe selection.
- Character collection.
- Upgrade section.
- Settings.
- Coins balance.
- Player profile.

Gameplay Interface

Display:

- Current score.
- Distance in meters.
- Coin counter.
- Energy meter.
- Health indicator.
- Chaser proximity.
- Ability button.
- Ultimate Mode button.
- Pause button.

Pause Menu

Include:

- Resume.
- Restart.
- Return to Main Menu.
- Sound settings.

Game Over Screen

Display:

- Final score.
- Distance travelled.
- Coins collected.
- Energy collected.
- Obstacles avoided.
- Bosses defeated.
- Best score.
- Retry button.
- Main Menu button.

UI Design Requirements

Use:

- Professional typography.
- Clear icons.
- Anime-inspired visual effects.
- Readable contrast.
- Smooth transitions.
- Appropriate spacing.
- Responsive layouts.

Do not use completely black backgrounds that hide interface elements.

Do not allow UI layers to block gameplay or touch controls.

Every visible button must be functional.

---

15. CHARACTER COLLECTION AND UPGRADE SYSTEM

Create a persistent progression system.

Players should be able to:

- Unlock characters.
- Purchase skins.
- Upgrade speed.
- Upgrade ability duration.
- Reduce cooldown.
- Increase starting protection.
- Unlock additional universes.

Every upgrade must produce a measurable gameplay effect.

Display:

- Current upgrade level.
- Upgrade cost.
- Current statistics.
- Improved statistics.
- Unlock requirements.

Do not create buttons that claim to purchase or upgrade something without actually changing the relevant game data.

---

16. AUDIO AND VISUAL EFFECTS

Audio

Implement:

- Main menu soundtrack.
- Universe-specific background music.
- Running sounds.
- Jump sounds.
- Slide sounds.
- Collision sounds.
- Coin collection sounds.
- Ability sounds.
- Boss battle music.
- Game Over sound.

Music should change appropriately between menus, running gameplay, Ultimate Mode, and boss encounters.

Provide independent music and sound effect volume controls.

Visual Effects

Implement:

- Anime-style aura effects.
- Motion trails.
- Energy particles.
- Speed effects.
- Impact effects.
- Landing effects.
- Ability animations.
- Ultimate transformation effects.
- Boss attack effects.

Use appropriate lighting and visual effects without sacrificing performance.

---

17. MOBILE-FIRST DEVELOPMENT

The game must be optimized primarily for Android smartphones.

Screen Orientation

Use portrait orientation (9:16) as the primary gameplay layout.

The game should occupy the available screen without unnecessary scrolling.

Mobile Controls

Implement reliable touch gesture detection.

Important:

- Detect swipe direction accurately.
- Avoid triggering multiple movements from one swipe.
- Prevent accidental browser scrolling during gameplay.
- Avoid conflicts between swipe controls and UI buttons.
- Provide responsive touch feedback.

Mobile UI

Position gameplay buttons where they are easily accessible.

Ensure:

- Score is readable.
- Energy bar is visible.
- Ability buttons are sufficiently large.
- Pause button is accessible.
- The character and obstacles remain visible.

Performance

Target smooth 60 FPS gameplay on capable mobile devices.

Use adaptive graphics settings for lower-end devices.

Optimize:

- Texture sizes.
- Model complexity.
- Draw calls.
- Particle counts.
- Memory consumption.
- Animation processing.
- Object spawning.

Avoid unnecessary rendering and excessive effects.

---

18. TECHNICAL ARCHITECTURE

Before implementation, inspect the existing project and identify its framework, rendering engine, dependencies, file structure, and existing assets.

Do not blindly overwrite working code.

Preserve useful existing functionality and rebuild broken systems properly.

Organize the project into logical modules.

Suggested architecture:

- GameManager
- GameStateManager
- PlayerController
- PlayerAnimationController
- PlayerPhysics
- LaneMovementController
- InputController
- ObstacleManager
- ObstaclePool
- CollisionManager
- EnemyChaserController
- AbilityManager
- UltimateModeManager
- CollectibleManager
- EnergyManager
- ScoreManager
- BossManager
- CharacterManager
- UniverseManager
- AudioManager
- CameraController
- UIManager
- SaveManager
- PerformanceManager

Use the architecture appropriate to the existing technology stack.

Main Game Loop

The game loop must correctly handle:

1. Reading player input.
2. Updating player movement.
3. Updating physics.
4. Updating animations.
5. Updating obstacle positions.
6. Spawning obstacles.
7. Updating enemy AI.
8. Checking collisions.
9. Updating collectibles.
10. Updating score and distance.
11. Updating energy and health.
12. Updating camera.
13. Rendering the scene.
14. Updating the UI.

Use delta time and proper game state management.

Game States

Implement these states:

- Loading
- Main Menu
- Character Selection
- Universe Selection
- Ready
- Playing
- Paused
- Boss Battle
- Game Over

Transitions must be handled correctly.

Prevent multiple simultaneous game loops.

Prevent gameplay updates while paused.

Restarting must reset the previous run's temporary objects, timers, score, collision states, and player physics.

---

19. CRITICAL BUG PREVENTION AND QUALITY ASSURANCE

Previous versions of this project repeatedly suffered from the following issues:

1. Completely black interfaces.
2. Missing character artwork.
3. Missing environment assets.
4. Start button not working.
5. Only the background appearing.
6. Static player character.
7. No running animation.
8. No actual movement.
9. No obstacles.
10. No collision detection.
11. No enemy chasing.
12. Broken mobile controls.
13. UI elements covering the gameplay.
14. Incorrect rendering order.
15. Missing asset references.
16. Runtime errors.
17. Incorrect initialization.
18. Restart button failing.
19. Gameplay freezing.
20. Excessive memory consumption.

These problems must be specifically tested for and eliminated.

Asset Loading

Implement:

- Asset preloading.
- Loading progress indicator.
- Asset validation.
- Error handling.
- Fallback assets.

Never allow a missing external image to turn the entire game screen black.

If an asset fails to load, use a visible fallback asset and report the problem.

Rendering Validation

Before starting a run, verify that:

- Renderer is initialized.
- Camera is active.
- Environment exists.
- Player exists.
- Player animation controller exists.
- Enemy exists.
- Game loop is active.
- Required UI elements are visible.

Do not start gameplay if essential systems have failed silently.

Functional Testing

Test the following:

TEST 1: Open the game and verify the main menu.

TEST 2: Open character selection and select different characters.

TEST 3: Change the universe and verify that the environment changes.

TEST 4: Press Start and verify that a playable character spawns.

TEST 5: Verify that running animation plays continuously.

TEST 6: Test all three lanes.

TEST 7: Test jumping and landing.

TEST 8: Test sliding.

TEST 9: Verify that obstacles spawn dynamically.

TEST 10: Verify that collision detection works.

TEST 11: Verify that the chasing enemy follows the player.

TEST 12: Collect coins and energy shards.

TEST 13: Activate character-specific abilities.

TEST 14: Fill the energy bar and activate Ultimate Mode.

TEST 15: Verify distance and score calculations.

TEST 16: Test pause and resume.

TEST 17: Test Game Over.

TEST 18: Test restart.

TEST 19: Test saving and loading progression.

TEST 20: Verify that the game works on a mobile screen.

Fix all discovered errors before considering the game complete.

---

20. DEVELOPMENT PRIORITIES

Implement the project in the following order.

PHASE 1 — FUNCTIONAL FOUNDATION

Build:

- Rendering engine.
- Main menu.
- Game state manager.
- Player spawning.
- Actual character movement.
- Running animation.
- Three-lane system.
- Jumping and sliding.
- Camera.

At the end of this phase, a complete basic endless runner must already be playable.

PHASE 2 — CORE GAMEPLAY

Build:

- Physics.
- Obstacles.
- Collision detection.
- Chasing enemy.
- Distance tracking.
- Score.
- Health.
- Game Over.
- Restart.

PHASE 3 — ANIME SYSTEMS

Build:

- Character selection.
- Universe selection.
- Universe-specific environments.
- Enemy variations.
- Character-specific animations.
- Special abilities.
- Ultimate Mode.

PHASE 4 — ADVANCED GAMEPLAY

Build:

- Coins.
- Energy shards.
- Power-ups.
- Boss encounters.
- Character collection.
- Upgrade system.
- Skins.
- Rewards.

PHASE 5 — POLISH AND OPTIMIZATION

Build:

- Professional UI.
- Soundtrack.
- Visual effects.
- Mobile controls.
- Responsive layouts.
- Performance optimization.
- Persistent saving.
- Final testing.

Do not skip the functional foundation in order to prioritize artwork or visual presentation.

---

21. FUTURE MULTIPLAYER EXPANSION

Design the architecture so multiplayer can be introduced later without rebuilding the entire game.

Potential future modes:

- 1v1 Survival Race.
- Team Escape.
- Cooperative Boss Raid.
- Global Leaderboards.

These features are future development goals and must not interfere with the quality of the current single-player version.

---

22. FINAL DELIVERY REQUIREMENTS

The final product must be a fully playable, properly implemented game.

When the user opens the project:

1. The main menu must load correctly.
2. Character selection must work.
3. Universe selection must work.
4. Start must load an actual gameplay scene.
5. The selected character must spawn and run automatically.
6. Running, jumping, and sliding animations must work.
7. All three lanes must be functional.
8. Obstacles must spawn dynamically.
9. Collision detection must work.
10. The chasing enemy must follow the player.
11. Coins and energy shards must be collectible.
12. Abilities must have real gameplay effects.
13. The score and distance must update continuously.
14. The pause and restart systems must work.
15. Game Over must function correctly.
16. Progression must be saved.
17. The game must work on Android mobile screens.

NON-NEGOTIABLE RULES

- Do not create a static visual mockup.
- Do not simulate gameplay using only background movement.
- Do not use a single static character image as the player.
- Do not create decorative buttons without functionality.
- Do not leave essential gameplay systems as placeholders.
- Do not claim that a feature works without implementing and testing it.
- Do not ignore runtime errors.
- Do not leave the game in a black-screen or incomplete state.
- Do not stop after creating the home screen.
- Do not sacrifice actual functionality for visual appearance.

If an advanced feature cannot be completed immediately, prioritize a functional implementation with clear limitations rather than displaying a fake feature.

FINAL INSTRUCTION

First inspect the existing project. Then implement the game systematically, beginning with a genuinely playable endless runner foundation.

After implementation, run the project, test the actual gameplay, identify errors, and fix them.

Do not merely provide an implementation plan, code snippets, screenshots, or a description of what you would build.

Modify the actual project files and deliver the working game.

The final result should feel like a polished, professional anime action game with smooth controls, genuine character animations, responsive gameplay, dynamic environments, exciting combat abilities, and a complete progression system.

Remember: A visually attractive game that cannot actually be played is a failed deliverable. Functionality, stability, and genuine gameplay take priority over everything else.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

## Objective
- Build and test a playable Android-first endless runner, **ANIME RUSH: MULTIVERSE ESCAPE**, by modifying the existing project.

- Run the project, test gameplay, fix discovered errors, and avoid claiming untested features work.

- Built a self-contained HTML/CSS/Canvas game without external game-engine dependencies or external artwork.
- Used original canvas-drawn character and environment visuals as fallback artwork.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added game UI, responsive styling, canvas gameplay, selection menus, upgrades, localStorage progression, controls, obstacles, collectibles, abilities, Ultimate Mode, boss flow, pause/restart, and score display.

## Objective
- Build and test a playable Android-first endless runner, **ANIME RUSH: MULTIVERSE ESCAPE**, by modifying the existing project.
- Deliver functional gameplay and progression, not just a visual mockup.

## Requirements
- Implement three-lane movement, jumping/sliding, animation, obstacles and collisions, a chasing enemy, collectibles, abilities, Ultimate Mode, bosses, pause/restart, and saved progression.
- Provide working character and universe selection that affect gameplay; support mobile portrait and desktop controls.
- Run the project, test gameplay, fix discovered errors, and avoid claiming untested features work.

## Decisions
- Built a self-contained HTML/CSS/Canvas game without external game-engine dependencies or external artwork.
- Used original canvas-drawn character and environment visuals as fallback artwork.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game UI, responsive styling, canvas gameplay, selection menus, upgrades, localStorage progression, controls, obstacles, collectibles, abilities, Ultimate Mode, boss flow, pause/restart, and score display.
- Added chase-pressure HUD, starting shields, boss lane warnings and dodge damage, improved runner/lane alignment, boss pause/resume, and a data-URI favicon.
- Removed misleading character lock badges; all roster choices are selectable.
- Fixed lane movement during boss fights; `node --check game.js` passes.
- Browser-tested at 390×844: universe selector shows four options, gameplay advances, keyboard controls and ability button respond, pause/resume/restart/menu work, and the canvas uses the full viewport.
- Tested Game Over and saved progression; best score persisted in `animeRushSave`.
- Captured and inspected mobile menu, gameplay, and Game Over screenshots under `/tmp/opencode/`.
- Latest browser console check showed no errors or warnings.

### Active
- Continue testing mobile swipe gestures, collision/jump/slide outcomes, boss encounter and defeat, and Ultimate Mode activation.
- Consider distinct character artwork and audio; current characters are generated canvas silhouettes and sound toggle is UI-only.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Test touch swipe movement, jumping/sliding, obstacle collision, and collectible/energy behavior.
2. Exercise boss intro, telegraphed attacks, ability damage, victory/defeat, and Ultimate Mode; fix any issues found.
3. Re-run syntax and browser-console checks and report verified versus unverified behavior.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game loop, rendering, controls, progression, collisions, and boss logic.
- `index.html`: Game UI, HUD, overlays, and favicon.
- `style.css`: Responsive menu, selection, HUD, and overlay styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project is served at `http://localhost:3002`.
- Playwright browser is open at the 390×844 mobile viewport.
- Character figures remain generated canvas silhouettes rather than distinct character artwork; no audio implementation is confirmed.
